easy.def: Having to do with a very strong kind of power.
examples: Nuclear power makes electricity.
The nuclear plant gives power to the town.
Nuclear power is very strong.

more.def: Having to do with the power that comes from splitting the tiny centers of atoms.
examples: A nuclear power plant makes electricity for the city.
Scientists study nuclear energy.
The sun's heat comes from nuclear reactions.

easy.def: The middle part of a cell.
examples: The cell has a nucleus.
The nucleus is in the middle.
We drew a nucleus.

more.def: The central part of a cell or an atom, which controls what it does.
examples: The nucleus is the control center of a cell.
The atom has a tiny nucleus at its center.
We drew a cell with a round nucleus.

easy.def: To push gently.
examples: I nudge my friend.
She nudged me.
The dog nudged my hand.

more.def: To push someone or something gently with your elbow or hand.
examples: I nudged my friend to wake her up.
She nudged me when it was my turn.
The puppy nudged my hand for a pat.

easy.def: A small lump of something, like gold.
examples: He found a gold nugget.
A nugget of gold.
I ate a chicken nugget.

more.def: A small, rough lump of something valuable, such as gold, or a small piece of food.
examples: The miner found a shiny nugget of gold in the river.
She ate a chicken nugget dipped in sauce.
The teacher gave us a nugget of advice: read every day.

easy.def: Something that annoys you.
examples: The fly is a nuisance.
The noise is a nuisance.
A nuisance.

more.def: A person or thing that is annoying or causes trouble.
examples: The fly in the kitchen was a nuisance.
The loud noise was a nuisance when I was reading.
Weeds are a nuisance in the garden.

easy.def: Not able to feel.
examples: My fingers are numb.
His foot was numb.
The cold made my toes numb.

more.def: Not able to feel anything in a part of your body.
examples: My fingers were numb from the cold.
His foot went numb after sitting too long.
The dentist made my mouth numb.

easy.def: A word or sign used to count.
examples: My number is seven.
Write the number.
Pick a number.

more.def: A word or sign that tells how many, such as 4 or twelve.
examples: The number on my door is twelve.
Pick a number between one and ten.
She wrote down the phone number on a card.

easy.def: How many there are.
examples: A big number came.
The number of kids is ten.
What is the number?

more.def: A total amount of people or things.
examples: A large number of birds gathered at the lake.
The number of students in our class is twenty-four.
A small number of cookies were left.

easy.def: Many.
examples: We saw numerous birds.
There were numerous stars.
Numerous kids came.

more.def: Very many; a lot of.
examples: We saw numerous birds at the lake.
Numerous stars filled the night sky.
She has visited the museum on numerous occasions.

easy.def: A woman who lives in a religious group and has given her life to prayer.
examples: The nun lives at the church.
A nun taught at the school.
The nun prays every day.

more.def: A woman who belongs to a religious community and lives a life of prayer and service.
examples: The nun taught at the school for many years.
The nuns work in a quiet house near the church.
The nun wore a long robe and a veil.

easy.def: A person who helps doctors take care of sick people.
examples: The nurse took my temperature.
A nurse helped me.
My aunt is a nurse.

more.def: A person trained to take care of people who are sick or hurt.
examples: The nurse checked my temperature.
A nurse bandaged his knee.
My aunt is a nurse at the hospital.

easy.def: To take care of a sick person.
examples: She nursed her brother.
Mom nursed me when I was sick.
The vet nursed the bird.

more.def: To take care of someone who is sick or hurt.
examples: Mom nursed me back to health when I had the flu.
She nursed the injured bird until it could fly.
He nursed his sore ankle.

easy.def: A woman who cares for children.
examples: The nursemaid sang to the baby.
A nursemaid watched the kids.
The nursemaid was kind.

more.def: A woman hired to take care of young children, in old stories.
examples: In the story, the nursemaid sang to the baby.
A nursemaid watched the children play.
The queen hired a nursemaid for the prince.

easy.def: A room for a baby.
examples: The baby is in the nursery.
The nursery is yellow.
Mom painted the nursery.

more.def: A room in a home that is set up for a baby.
examples: The baby slept quietly in the nursery.
Mom painted the nursery a soft yellow.
The nursery had a crib, a rocking chair and a toy chest.

easy.def: A place that grows and sells plants.
examples: We bought a tree at the nursery.
The nursery has many flowers.
Dad went to the nursery.

more.def: A place where young plants and trees are grown to be sold.
examples: We bought a young apple tree at the nursery.
The nursery had rows of flowers and small bushes.
Dad asked the worker at the nursery which plants grow best in shade.

easy.def: The work of a nurse.
examples: She studies nursing.
Nursing is a caring job.
My aunt works in nursing.

more.def: The job of caring for sick people in a hospital or at home.
examples: She studies nursing at college.
She went to college to study nursing.
My aunt works in nursing at the hospital.

easy.def: To help something grow and be healthy.
examples: Plants need water to nurture them.
She nurtures the baby bird.
We nurtured the seed.

more.def: To care for and help someone or something grow and be strong.
examples: A gardener nurtures seedlings with water and sunlight.
Parents nurture their children with love and care.
The teacher tried to nurture each child's talents.

easy.def: A hard seed in a shell.
examples: Squirrels eat nuts.
The nut is hard.
I cracked a nut.

more.def: A seed or fruit with a hard shell that grows on some trees.
examples: A squirrel stored a nut in the tree.
Walnuts and almonds are nuts.
We cracked the nuts with a nutcracker.

easy.def: A small piece of metal that fits on a bolt.
examples: Dad used a nut and bolt.
Tighten the nut.
The nut is loose.

more.def: A small metal piece with a hole in the middle that screws onto a bolt.
examples: The nut on the wheel was loose.
Dad tightened the nut with a wrench.
A nut and bolt hold the chair together.

easy.def: A tool for cracking nuts.
examples: Dad used a nutcracker.
The nutcracker cracks nuts.
A nutcracker is a tool.

more.def: A tool used to crack the hard shells of nuts.
examples: Dad used a nutcracker to open the walnuts.
The nutcracker is carved like a soldier.
We watched the ballet The Nutcracker.

easy.def: A spice used in baking.
examples: Mom added nutmeg.
Nutmeg smells good.
The cookies have nutmeg.

more.def: A brown spice made from the seed of a tropical tree, used in baking.
examples: Mom sprinkled nutmeg on the eggnog.
Nutmeg gives the pie a warm flavor.
The pumpkin cake had cinnamon and nutmeg.

easy.def: Something in food that helps you grow.
examples: Milk has nutrients for strong bones.
Good food has nutrients.
Plants get nutrients from dirt.

more.def: A substance that living things need in order to grow and stay healthy.
examples: Plants take in nutrients from the soil through their roots.
Vegetables are full of important nutrients.
Fertilizer adds nutrients to the soil.

easy.def: The food that keeps your body healthy.
examples: Good nutrition helps you grow.
Fruit is good nutrition.
We learned about nutrition.

more.def: The food a body needs to grow and stay healthy, or the study of that food.
examples: Good nutrition helps children grow strong.
We learned about nutrition in health class.
Fruits and vegetables give your body good nutrition.

easy.def: Good for your body.
examples: Fruit is nutritious.
A nutritious lunch.
Milk is nutritious.

more.def: Full of what the body needs to grow and be healthy.
examples: Fruit and vegetables are nutritious.
She packed a nutritious lunch with fruit and nuts.
Milk is a nutritious drink for children.

easy.def: The hard outside of a nut.
examples: A mouse hid in a nutshell.
The nutshell is hard.
I cracked a nutshell.

more.def: The hard outer covering of a nut.
examples: A tiny doll's bed was made from a nutshell.
A tiny boat was made from a half nutshell.
In a nutshell means in a few words.

easy.def: Tasting like nuts or full of nuts.
examples: The cake is nutty.
I like a nutty bread.
The cookies taste nutty.

more.def: Tasting like nuts, or full of nuts.
examples: The bread had a nutty taste.
The nutty cookies were full of walnuts.
I love the nutty smell of toasted almonds.

easy.def: Silly or very odd.
examples: That is a nutty idea.
She told a nutty joke.
A nutty dance.

more.def: Very silly, odd or crazy in a fun way.
examples: That is a nutty idea, but it might work.
She told a nutty joke that made us all laugh.
The nutty professor in the cartoon wears mismatched socks.

easy.def: To rub or press against something with your nose.
examples: The horse nuzzles my hand.
The puppy nuzzled me.
The cat nuzzled her.

more.def: To rub or press gently with the nose or face.
examples: The horse nuzzled my hand, looking for a treat.
The puppy nuzzled up against me.
The cat nuzzled her face against my arm.
